newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends higher on US cold weather forecasts.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends higher on US cold weather forecasts.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil ended Wednesday on the day's highs gaining ground on news of continued cold weather in the U.S and support from bullish U.S stocks data
"Its on the weather and on the lost downside (on the stock data)," said one trader.
February IPE Brent closed up 21 cents at $24.80 a barrel, breaching rather than breaking resistance at $24.70.
The front month Brent contract made a late mini-rally towards the close having recovered earlier losses which were prompted by selling on NYMEX products.
"Heating, gasoline and WTI led the way and Brent followed," said one IPE floor trader.
Traders said the downside caused by bearish API and EIA U.S data had not been followed through. NYMEX heating oil and gasoline both recovered in the second half of the day.
A second cold snap was seen prolonging cold temperatures in the Midwest and Northeast, a reversal of earlier forecasts of milder weather to come.
"The forecast of cold weather beat the inventories," said one broker.

IPE gas oil had ended the day earlier broadly unchanged, up 75 cents at $230.50 a tonne. The Jan/Feb backwardation was up $1 at $4.50 garnering support from the continued cold weather gripping much of Europe.
